parser.title: Book parsing method

descriptions.spacy: Poorly understands context and may get confused by complex sentences
descriptions.spacy_llm: Nearly as accurate as Pro, but a bit faster
descriptions.llm: Understands context well and identifies characters well

spacy.simple_dialogs: Works well with simple dialogues where the speaker is named directly
spacy.complex_dialogs: More likely to misidentify the speaker in complex dialogues

spacy_llm.accuracy: spaCy handles simple lines where the speaker is named directly, AI handles the rest
spacy_llm.cost: About 15% cheaper than Pro with nearly the same accuracy
spacy_llm.duration: Takes longer than Lite, but a bit less than Pro

llm.accuracy: More accurately identifies characters and who is speaking
llm.unnamed_speakers: Handles dialogues better where the speaker is not named directly
llm.duration: Processing takes longer: roughly 1–2.5 min more per 1 MB of text

lines.system_title: Book: Alice in Wonderland (AI Version, Tea Party Included)
lines.line1_text: Whoa! I just wanted to flip through a book, and it texted me "heyyy". What is happening?!
lines.line1_meta: — the Guest dropped a sandwich. Butter side down, naturally.
lines.line2_text: Welcome down the rabbit hole! This app turns an ordinary book into a chat. Now the characters answer back instead of napping on a shelf!
lines.line2_meta: — Alice shrank to the size of an emoji.
lines.line3_text: So I can message the Mad Hatter and he'll actually reply?
lines.line3_meta: — the Guest sniffed their teacup suspiciously.
lines.line4_text: He will! With a riddle about a raven and a writing desk. Blocking him is useless, he's already celebrating your unbirthday in your DMs.
lines.line4_meta: — the Cheshire Cat left a 😁 reaction and vanished. The reaction stayed.
lines.line5_text: That's it, I'm signing in with Google before the White Rabbit grabs my nickname!
lines.line5_meta: — the Guest shouted and dove finger-first at the button.

lines.system_title: Book: A Space Odyssey: Where Are My Socks (AI Version)
lines.line1_text: Computer, there's an unknown button on the screen! Alien attack or another update?
lines.line1_meta: — the Captain heroically hid behind the coffee machine.
lines.line2_text: Worse, Captain. It's an app that turns books into live chats. The crew might start reading.
lines.line2_meta: — the Onboard AI switched on the alarm lights. Very stylish ones.
lines.line3_text: So instead of an 800-page airlock manual, I can just ask a character where the "don't die" button is?
lines.line3_meta: — the Captain carefully moved an elbow away from the red lever.
lines.line4_text: Confirmed. Characters reply in character. Unlike your first officer, they don't pretend the signal and their conscience got lost.
lines.line4_meta: — the AI displayed a graph of crew laziness. It didn't fit on the screen.
lines.line5_text: Launch Google sign-in! And tell no one I cried over a novel about a lonely Mars rover.
lines.line5_meta: — the Captain ordered, wiping a tear with a spacesuit sleeve.

lines.system_title: Book: Sherlock Holmes and the Case of the Unfinished Book (AI Version)
lines.line1_text: Holmes, this book just sent me a message! Shall I call the police or an exorcist?
lines.line1_meta: — Watson waved a rolled-up newspaper at the monitor.
lines.line2_text: Elementary, Watson! The app has turned the text into a chat. By the way, you got stuck on page three last year.
lines.line2_meta: — Holmes eyed the dust and biscuit crumbs on the cover.
lines.line3_text: How did you know?! Wait... Can I now simply ask the characters who the murderer is?
lines.line3_meta: — Watson was so thrilled that his moustache wiggled.
lines.line4_text: You may ask. But the suspects now answer personally: they lie, take offence and demand lawyers. A splendid evening!
lines.line4_meta: — Holmes played a happy tune on the violin. The neighbours banged on the wall.
lines.line5_text: I'm hitting the Google button! I want to ask Moriarty if he ate my pudding!
lines.line5_meta: — Watson lunged for the mouse and tripped over Holmes's skull.

lines.system_title: Book: Dracula. Late Night Texts (AI Version)
lines.line1_text: Good evening... Wow, it's 3 a.m. and the character is online. Do you ever sleep?
lines.line1_meta: — whispered the Guest, pulling the blanket up to their nose.
lines.line2_text: In the daytime! This delightful app turned my novel into a chat. At last, guests come on their own. No carriage, no wolves.
lines.line2_meta: — Dracula adjusted his collar and dropped his phone into the coffin.
lines.line3_text: Hold on, I can talk to you instead of just reading about you scaring lawyers?
lines.line3_meta: — the Guest ate a clove of garlic, just in case.
lines.line4_text: Precisely! Ask me anything: about the castle, the mortgage on the castle, or why I never show up in selfies.
lines.line4_meta: — Dracula sent 27 bats instead of a sticker.
lines.line5_text: Fine, I'm signing in with Google. But I am not coming to dinner, don't even ask!
lines.line5_meta: — the Guest clicked the button, still clutching a wooden toothpick.

lines.system_title: Book: Romeo and Juliet: Seen at 11:59 PM (AI Version)
lines.line1_text: Juliet! I've been under your balcony half the night, and you're in some chat?
lines.line1_meta: — Romeo sneezed as romantically as he could.
lines.line2_text: Darling, the app turned our tragedy into text messages. No more yelling across all of Verona!
lines.line2_meta: — Juliet snuggled into a blanket with a plate of lasagne.
lines.line3_text: So a reader can jump in and tell us: "Stop, first check whether she's just asleep"?
lines.line3_meta: — Romeo stopped to think for the first time in the whole play.
lines.line4_text: Yes! You can question the characters, argue and give advice. Tybalt has already learned to send angry emojis instead of drawing his sword.
lines.line4_meta: — Juliet added a ❤️ reaction, and the Nurse took a screenshot.
lines.line5_text: Signing in with Google right now! Just don't give your parents the balcony password.
lines.line5_meta: — Romeo hit the button and tumbled into a rose bush.

lines.system_title: Book: Don Quixote vs. the Wi-Fi (AI Version)
lines.line1_text: Master, lower your lance! That's no wizard, that's a router. And there's some chat on the screen.
lines.line1_meta: — Sancho shielded the electronics and his sausage.
lines.line2_text: My faithful Sancho! This magic mirror turns books into conversations. Now my heroic deeds can argue with me!
lines.line2_meta: — Don Quixote solemnly put a washbasin on his head.
lines.line3_text: So people can text you directly and explain that the giants are windmills?
lines.line3_meta: — Sancho stopped chewing, full of hope.
lines.line4_text: Let them! Every soul shall receive a knightly reply, a lengthy speech and possibly a challenge to a duel.
lines.line4_meta: — Rocinante quietly lay down, for the speech had begun.
lines.line5_text: I'm signing in with Google before you knight our microwave!
lines.line5_meta: — Sancho poked the button with a greasy sausage finger.

lines.system_title: Book: Little Red Riding Hood. The Wolf Is Online (AI Version)
lines.line1_text: Grandma, why do you have such a strange username: "FluffyTail2000"?
lines.line1_meta: — Red Riding Hood squinted over her basket of pies.
lines.line2_text: The better to chat with you! This app turned the fairy tale into messages. Grandma... um... is writing from a new account.
lines.line2_meta: — the Wolf adjusted his nightcap and hiccuped loudly.
lines.line3_text: So I can skip the forest and grill the characters first?
lines.line3_meta: — Red opened a notebook titled "Suspicious Ears".
lines.line4_text: Sadly, yes. Ask about ears, eyes, teeth. Just don't ask where Grandma is, it upsets my stomach.
lines.line4_meta: — someone inside the Wolf sent a voice message about slippers.
lines.line5_text: I'm signing in with Google and adding the Huntsman to the chat!
lines.line5_meta: — Red pressed the button, and the Wolf urgently went offline.

lines.system_title: Book: The Great Watermelon Heist. A Twilight Episode (AI Version)
lines.line1_text: Gentlemen, this is the fourth time we've stolen this watermelon. The moment we get it over the fence, it's back in the patch!
lines.line1_meta: — Fayst whispered. The clock said 3:00 a.m. It had been saying that for two weeks.
lines.line2_text: I have worse news. I was dozing on lookout when an app that turns books into live chats opened by itself. The book is called "Three Thieves and One Watermelon".
lines.line2_meta: — PjSm switched on his slipper headlights. There were three thieves. For some reason, four shadows.
lines.line3_text: Great book! Some klutz in it drops the watermelon on his own foot. What a doofus... Ouch!
lines.line3_meta: — Mac's phone said "Thud!" exactly one second before the thud.
lines.line4_text: It knows everything about us! Even that my stocking has a hole, and our heist plan is drawn on the back of a receipt!
lines.line4_meta: — Fayst turned so pale that the moon saw him as competition.
lines.line5_text: Stay calm. It's a live chat, so let's ask the characters how this ends. Admittedly, the characters are us.
lines.line5_meta: — the screen blinked "Fayst is typing...", though Fayst was holding the watermelon with both hands.
lines.line6_text: We've got a reply! "Put the watermelon back." Sent from my number. Tomorrow.
lines.line6_meta: — Mac waved cheerfully into the darkness. The darkness thought about it and waved back.
lines.line7_text: That's it, we're quitting crime! I'm signing in with Google to read something calming. Ghost stories, for instance.
lines.line7_meta: — the three losers got home empty-handed. The watermelon was waiting in the kitchen. With a bookmark in it.

lines.system_title: Book: 2112. Jenny Flint and the Scrap Metal Rocket (AI Version)
lines.line1_text: It's the year 2112. The Priests of the Temples decide what we read, sing and eat for breakfast. So I'm building a rocket out of scrap!
lines.line1_meta: — whispered Jenny Flint, bolting a washing machine to the hull.
lines.line2_text: Attention! Unauthorised rocket detected. Reminder: all dreams must be approved by the Priests three years in advance.
lines.line2_meta: — droned the Temple Computer in a voice as dull as an iron manual.
lines.line3_text: Too late. I found an old guitar in a cave behind the waterfall. One strum, and I caught an opinion of my own!
lines.line3_meta: — Jenny Flint played a chord. Out of tune, but his.
lines.line4_text: Personal opinions are forbidden. Hand the guitar to the Priests, and they will carefully step on it.
lines.line4_meta: — a "NOT APPROVED" stamp appeared on every screen on the planet.
lines.line5_text: Try this first: an app that turns books into live chats. The characters reply in character and never ask the Priests for permission.
lines.line5_meta: — Jenny Flint plugged his phone into the main console.
lines.line6_text: Analysing... I have just chatted with a pirate from a book. He called me a teapot. I liked it! Is there a spare seat on that rocket?
lines.line6_meta: — for the first time in a century, the Temple Computer blinked pink.
lines.line7_text: You can ride in my phone. I'm signing in with Google, and we launch while the Priests are at lunch!
lines.line7_meta: — the rocket roared, sneezed washing powder and carried the rebels off to the stars.
